newsitem.title: USA: Apple cuts prices on Power Mac computers.
newsitem.headline: Apple cuts prices on Power Mac computers.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc said Thursday it was cutting U.S. prices on most of its Power Macintosh personal computers by as much as 30 percent to make the machines more competitive with rival products.
The price cuts are part of Apple's effort to make its machines as attractive as so-called Wintel PCs -- machines based on Intel Corp microprocessors and running Microsoft Corp's Windows software.
Apple, based in Cupertino, said it was reducing the price of its high-end Power Macintosh 9500/200 to about $4,200 from $4,900.
The price of the entry-level Power Macintosh 7200/120 business machine will be cut to about $1,600 from $2,300, the company said. The price cuts range from 9 percent to 30 percent.

"Now when a business customer does a feature-for-feature comparison between a Power Macintosh and a Wintel machine, that customer will find the Power Macintosh competitively priced," Gary Little, Apple's senior vice president of the Power Macintosh division, said in a statement.
Apple's computers have traditionally been priced higher than PCs with similar features made by companies such as International Business Machines Corp and Compaq Computer Corp.

With the release of Microsoft's Windows 95 program a year ago, Apple lost much of its bragging rights for ease of use. To make its machines more attractive, the company has had to cut prices to keep customers from defecting.
An Apple spokeswoman said the company had already cut prices in other parts of the world.
